title: Pocket Parks and Rooftop Farms: Small Green Spaces, Big City Impact
title_zh: 袖珍公园和屋顶农场：小绿色空间，城市大影响
intro_zh: 本文约880词，含6个重点词，难度适中，适合CET-4水平。

paragraphs.en: In many modern cities, buildings of steel and concrete seem to spread endlessly. As people walk through busy streets, they often look for a place to escape the noise and enjoy some peace. Green spaces in cities are not just decorative; they play a vital role in improving the quality of urban life. From tiny pocket parks to green rooftop farms, these natural areas offer residents a chance to reconnect with the environment. In recent years, more city planners have begun to recognize that even small patches of green can bring huge benefits to physical health, mental relaxation, and social connection. This article explores how these 'green oases' are changing the face of our cities.
paragraphs.zh: 在许多现代城市，钢铁和混凝土的建筑似乎无尽地延伸。当人们走过繁忙的街道时，他们常常寻找一个逃离噪音、享受宁静的地方。城市中的绿色空间不仅仅是装饰性的；它们在提高城市生活质量方面发挥着至关重要的作用。从袖珍公园到绿色屋顶农场，这些自然区域为居民提供了重新与自然联系的机会。近年来，越来越多的城市规划者开始认识到，即使是一小块绿色也能为身体健康、心理放松和社会联系带来巨大好处。本文探讨了这些“绿色绿洲”如何改变我们城市的面貌。

paragraphs.en: One of the most successful ideas in urban design is the pocket park. A pocket park is a small public green space, often no larger than a tennis court. It can be tucked between buildings, on a street corner, or even in an empty lot. New York City's Paley Park, opened in 1967, is a classic example. It occupies only about 390 square meters, yet it attracts thousands of visitors every day. With a famous waterfall wall and a few trees, the park offers a cool and calm break from the hot, noisy streets. Such small spaces prove that size does not matter when it comes to creating a pleasant environment.
paragraphs.zh: 城市设计中最成功的概念之一是袖珍公园。袖珍公园是小型公共绿色空间，通常不超过一个网球场大小。它可以藏于建筑物之间、街角，甚至荒地。纽约市的佩利公园于1967年开放，是一个经典范例。它仅占地约390平方米，却每天吸引数千名游客。公园内有一座著名的瀑布墙和几棵树，为炎热嘈杂的街道提供了一个凉爽宁静的休息之所。这样的小空间证明，在营造宜人环境方面，大小并不重要。

paragraphs.en: Beyond pocket parks, cities have started to use rooftops and walls to grow plants. Rooftop farms have become popular in places like Brooklyn, New York. The Brooklyn Grange is a rooftop farm that covers about 10,000 square meters. It produces more than 22 tons of fresh vegetables and herbs every year. In addition, vertical gardens are an eye-catching way to add greenery to tall buildings. By covering walls with climbing plants or special panels, these gardens reduce heat, improve air quality, and look beautiful. For example, the Bosco Verticale in Milan is a pair of residential towers covered with nearly 800 trees and thousands of plants. It is like a 'vertical forest' that helps to clean the air and provide habitats for birds.
paragraphs.zh: 除了袖珍公园，城市已开始利用屋顶和墙壁来种植植物。屋顶农场在纽约布鲁克林等地变得流行。布鲁克林农场是一个占地约一万平方米的屋顶农场，每年生产超过22吨新鲜蔬菜和草药。此外，垂直花园是为高层建筑增添绿意的引人注目的方式。通过用攀爬植物或特殊面板覆盖墙壁，这些花园可以降低热量，改善空气质量，看起来也很漂亮。例如，米兰的“垂直森林”是一对覆盖着近800棵树和数千株植物的住宅塔楼，就像一座“垂直森林”，有助于净化空气并为鸟类提供栖息地。

paragraphs.en: Another exciting trend is turning abandoned infrastructure into green public spaces. The High Line in New York City is a perfect example. It was once an elevated railway used to move goods, but it had been empty for decades. Instead of tearing it down, city residents and designers worked together to transform it into a beautiful walking path with native plants. Today, more than seven million people visit the High Line each year. This project not only preserves a piece of history but also creates a long green belt through the busy city. Similar projects have appeared in other cities, showing that unused spaces can have a second life.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个激动人心的趋势是将废弃的基础设施改造成绿色公共空间。纽约的高线公园是一个完美的例子。它曾经是一条用于运输货物的高架铁路，但已经空置了几十年。居民和设计师没有拆除它，而是合作将其改造成一条种满本地植物的美丽步行道。如今，每年有超过七百万游客参观高线公园。这个项目不仅保留了一段历史，还在繁忙城市中创造了一条长长的绿色地带。类似项目已出现在其他城市，表明未使用的空间可以有第二次生命。

paragraphs.en: Community gardens serve as more than just places to grow food. They bring neighbors together and create a sense of belonging. In many cities, people can rent a small plot of land to grow flowers, vegetables, and herbs. The garden becomes a social center where children learn about nature, elderly people share their wisdom, and new friends meet. For example, a study in Chicago found that neighborhoods with community gardens had lower crime rates. Another study showed that gardening can reduce stress and improve mood. The scent of fragrant herbs and the sight of colorful flowers make these gardens a true delight for the senses.
paragraphs.zh: 社区花园不仅仅是种植食物的地方。它们把邻居聚在一起，创造归属感。在许多城市，人们可以租一小块地来种植花卉、蔬菜和草药。花园成为社交中心，孩子们学习自然知识，老人分享智慧，新朋友们相遇。例如，芝加哥的一项研究发现，有社区花园的社区犯罪率更低。另一项研究表明，园艺可以减轻压力，改善情绪。芬芳药草的香气和五彩花朵的景象使这些花园成为感官的极大享受。

paragraphs.en: The environmental benefits of urban green spaces are impressive. Trees and plants absorb rainwater, reduce the heat island effect, and filter pollutants from the air. In summer, a shaded street can be several degrees cooler than a bare concrete road. Moreover, green spaces can produce food that is healthy and sustainable. Urban farmers harvest fresh vegetables and fruits just steps away from where people live, cutting the need for long-distance transport. A study from the University of Michigan estimated that a small green space can absorb hundreds of kilograms of carbon dioxide each year. These are simple, local solutions to global environmental problems.
paragraphs.zh: 城市绿色空间的环境效益令人惊叹。树木和植物吸收雨水，减少热岛效应，并过滤空气中的污染物。在夏天，一条有树荫的街道可能比光秃秃的混凝土道路凉爽好几度。此外，绿色空间可以生产健康且可持续的食物。城市农民就在居民生活几步之外的地方收获新鲜蔬菜和水果，减少了对长途运输的需求。密歇根大学的一项研究估计，一小片绿色空间每年可以吸收数百公斤的二氧化碳。这些都是解决全球环境问题的简单而本地的方案。

paragraphs.en: Cities are also building green corridors to link these scattered patches. In Singapore, a network of park connectors now covers over 300 kilometers, allowing people to walk or cycle through lush greenery across the island. Such connected green spaces help animals move safely and make it easier for residents to enjoy nature every day. The idea is simple: by joining small green areas together, a city can create a much larger living environment for both people and wildlife.
paragraphs.zh: 城市也在建设绿色走廊来连接这些分散的绿色区域。在新加坡，一个公园连接网络现已覆盖超过300公里，让人们可以穿过郁郁葱葱的绿色植物步行或骑行全岛。这种连接的绿色空间有助于动物安全移动，也方便居民每天享受自然。理念很简单：通过将小片绿地区域连接在一起，城市可以为人类和野生动物创造一个更大的生活环境。

paragraphs.en: Urban green spaces are no longer a luxury; they are a necessity for sustainable cities. Whether it is a pocket park, a rooftop farm, or a community garden, every small patch of green counts. These spaces improve physical health, boost mental well-being, strengthen social ties, and help the planet. As more people move into cities, we must find creative ways to integrate nature into our daily environment. Let us plant more trees, support local gardens, and value the beauty of green in the concrete world. In the end, a city with green spaces is a city with heart.
paragraphs.zh: 城市绿色空间不再是一种奢侈品，而是可持续城市的需要。无论是袖珍公园、屋顶农场还是社区花园，每一小块绿色都重要。这些空间改善身体健康，提升心理健康，加强社会联系，并帮助地球。随着更多人搬入城市，我们必须找到创造性的方法将自然融入我们的日常环境。让我们种植更多树木，支持本地花园，并珍视混凝土世界中的绿色之美。最终，一个拥有绿色空间的城市是一个有灵魂的城市。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Urban green spaces are expensive and hard to build.
Small green spaces can greatly improve urban life and the environment.
New York City has the best green spaces in the world.
People should move to the countryside to enjoy nature.
questions.explain: 主旨题。文章通篇讲口袋公园、屋顶农场等小型绿色空间如何改善城市生活质量、环境和社会联系，所以B正确。A错误，文中强调小而有效；C过于具体；D未提及。

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the High Line in New York?
options: It was originally a street for cars.
It was built recently and never used.
It was an old railway that has now become a walking path.
It is a rooftop farm in Brooklyn.
questions.explain: 细节题。第四段明确指出高线公园曾是一条废弃的高架铁路，后被改造为步行道，所以C正确。A、B、D均与原文不符。

questions.q: What does the author imply about community gardens?
options: They mainly provide space for elderly people to exercise.
They can help reduce crime and bring neighbors together.
They are only useful for growing food.
They cost a lot of money to build.
questions.explain: 推断题。第五段提到社区花园让邻居们聚在一起，且芝加哥研究显示有社区花园的社区犯罪率更低，所以B正确。A“主要为老年人锻炼”未提及；C“只对种食物有用”与原文矛盾；D“花费很多钱”未提及。

questions.q: The word 'tucked' in Paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: 词义题。tucked在原文中描述公园“藏于”建筑之间，意为“隐藏/安置在舒服的地方”，A最接近。B拿走；C装饰；D拆掉。
